business_description.value: Monster Beverage Corporation, through its subsidiaries, engages in development, marketing, sale, and distribution of energy drink beverages and concentrates in the United States and internationally. The company operates through four segments: Monster Energy Drinks, Strategic Brands, Alcohol Brands, and Other. It offers carbonated non-carbonated energy drinks, ready-to-drink iced teas, lemonades, juice cocktails, single-serve juices and fruit beverages, ready-to-drink dairy and coffee drinks, energy drinks, sports drinks and single-serve still waters, and sodas that are considered natural, sparkling juices, and flavored sparkling beverages. In addition, the company provides its products under the Monster Energy, Monster Energy Ultra, Rehab Monster, Monster Energy Nitro, Java Monster, Punch Monster, Juice Monster, Monster Tour Water, Reign Total Body Fuel, Reign Storm, Bang Energy, NOS, Full Throttle, Burn, Mother, Nalu, Ultra Energy, Play and Power Play, Relentless, BPM, BU, Samurai, Live+, Predator, and Fury brands. Further, it offers craft beers, flavored malt beverages,and hard seltzers under the Jai Alai IPA, Florida Man IPA, Dale’s Pale Ale, Wild Basin Hard Seltzers, Dallas Blonde, Deep Ellum IPA, Perrin Brewing Company Black Ale, Hop Rising Double IPA, Wasatch Apricot Hefeweizen, The Beast, and Beast Tea, Blind Lemon, and Blinder Lemon brands. The company engages in the concentrates and/or beverage bases to authorized bottling, and canning operations. It sells its products to full-service beverage bottlers/distributors, retail grocery and specialty chains, wholesalers, club stores, mass merchandisers, convenience and gas chains, food service customers, value stores, e-commerce retailers, and the military. The company was formerly known as Hansen Natural Corporation and changed its name to Monster Beverage Corporation in January 2012. Monster Beverage Corporation was founded in 1985 and is headquartered in Corona, California.

historical_forecast_error.estimate_type: final consensus before each result — CIQ Estimates→Surprise 'Estimate', Fiscal Years, company level
historical_forecast_error.eligibility_note: Each observation is the consensus on the eve of the result — lead time ~0 — so it measures last-mile surprise: a cross-check on scenario severity and on how wrong late consensus has been. It is NOT a distribution of how far consensus moves over a holding period; that needs point-in-time consensus snapshots, which no Estimates Report carries. Each 'actual' is the figure CIQ's Estimates set against its own consensus, which is often NOT the line the financial statements report; `accounting_basis` names the filer's accounting STANDARD (US GAAP, IFRS), never the basis of that actual.
historical_forecast_error.usage_note: EBIT- or EBITDA-level shock today: error_per_forecast_revenue × today's revenue consensus. Revenue × margin scenario: the SAME year's Revenue pct_error and ratio_error, kept together. ratio_error alone answers how wrong the margin (or capex-intensity) forecast was, and multiplied by revenue it drops the revenue miss's effect. Exact identity: error_per_forecast_revenue = ratio_error + (actual ÷ actual revenue) × (actual revenue ÷ forecast revenue − 1).

non_operating_assets.reason: the primary current and historical EV multiple series use the vendor's TEV definition, which carries non-operating investments inside enterprise value; carving them out of the bridge alone would value a different enterprise than the one the multiple was struck on
non_operating_assets.adjustment_condition: only if BOTH the current and the historical valuation series are rebuilt consistently on the adjusted operating-EV basis — a separate, consistently rebased framework, never a carve-out in the bridge alone

date_semantics.reference_date_semantics: the screening/reference date the page was assembled against — NOT the freshness date of its inputs; each input's own date is named in this block
date_semantics.analysis_as_of_rule: the latest of price_as_of, market_cap_as_of, tev_as_of, consensus_as_of (a '≥' date counts at its floor), balance_sheet_date and historical_multiple_latest_observation

data_quality_detail: vendor bridge: net_debt supplied by the CIQ workbook because EDGAR had no usable tag

margin.source: EDGAR companyfacts OperatingIncomeLoss / RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax — reported median over 10 FY

d_and_a.basis: consolidated trailing twelve months to 2026-06-30 (EDGAR: fiscal year + year-to-date − prior year-to-date)
d_and_a.source: EDGAR companyfacts DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization (fiscal year + year-to-date − prior year-to-date, to 2026-06-30)

net_debt.source: CIQ classified balance sheet (vendor basis; EDGAR debt tags absent or under-captured) [Monster Beverage Corporation NasdaqGS MNST Financials_Quarterly.xls sha cbf70bf218]

shares_outstanding.basis: point-in-time shares outstanding — the per-share denominator (item 24)
shares_outstanding.source: mechanical.stock_info.shares_out (EDGAR XBRL shares outstanding); 0.1% above the filer's basic weighted average 978,662,000 (2026-04-01..2026-06-30)

dilutive_increment.basis: diluted less basic weighted average over the latest 10-Q quarter — the dilution test

ltm_fcf.source: EDGAR companyfacts operating_cash_flow − capex (FY2025, same period)

anchor.note: ATTENTION FILTER, not a verdict. Even a firm anchor requires a full bear/base/bull 2:1 underwrite before any BUY. Spot and reward-to-base are computed live at triage, not stored here.

scenario_eligibility.reason: the active recipe is R1-family (R1_midcycle_margin_evebitda) and R1's anchor applies — these fields are an R1 record's inputs (its template reads `d_and_a` and `net_debt` from here)
